5.text:
Supertech Supernova Astralis vs Mahagun Mezzaria: Which is the safer buy?
My preliminary pick: Mahagun Mezzaria

If your priority is protecting your capital, getting a clean property title, avoiding legal complications and having a reliable exit option, I would lean towards Mahagun Mezzaria.

There is, however, one very important distinction: Supertech Supernova Astralis is registered as a commercial project, whereas Mahagun Mezzaria is a residential project. So this isn't a completely like-for-like comparison.

The biggest concern with Astralis isn't its location, architecture or potential rental yield. It is the legal and insolvency situation surrounding Supertech Realtors and the wider Supernova development.

1. The biggest difference: legal and financial risk
 

Supertech Supernova Astralis

High legal risk

UP-RERA registration: UPRERAPRJ7263.

Promoter: Supertech Realtors Pvt. Ltd.

Registered as an ongoing commercial project.

The wider Supernova project is under insolvency proceedings.

 

Mahagun Mezzaria

Relatively safer

UP-RERA registration: UPRERAPRJ3306.

Promoter: Nexgen Infracon Pvt. Ltd. (Mahagun Group).

Residential project.

No equivalent Supernova-style insolvency process identified in the records reviewed.

Sources: UP-RERA records for 
up-rera.in
+1
.

2. Why I am cautious about Astralis

There are several serious developments that a buyer should understand.

A. Supertech insolvency

In June 2024, NCLT initiated insolvency proceedings against Supertech Realtors in relation to Supernova following a Bank of Maharashtra claim involving approximately ₹168 crore.

On 16 December 2025, the Supreme Court constituted an empowered committee headed by former Justice M.M. Kumar to oversee the resolution of the project.

The committee has been involved in finding a new developer to complete the wider development. 
The Times of India
+1

B. Restrictions on property transactions

This is particularly important.

In 2026, the Supreme Court-appointed committee required prior written approval for property transactions involving Supertech Realtors' project. This includes sales, transfers and creation of third-party rights.

Transactions without the required approval can be treated as void. 
ETLegalWorld.com

This creates an additional complication for someone buying Astralis.

C. Operational issues

Supernova has also faced water-supply problems arising from outstanding dues to Noida Authority. Although supply was subsequently restored, outstanding infrastructure and management issues have been reported. 
The Times of India
+1

My assessment: Even if an Astralis unit is physically ready, that does not automatically make its title, transfer or resale process safe.

Booking an under-construction property today can be a good investment, but it also carries significant risks. The biggest danger is that you pay money now based on promises about a property that may not be delivered as promised.

If you're considering booking a flat, apartment, or house in an under-construction project in India, here are the things that could go wrong.

1. Major risks you should know
 

1. Project delays

The builder might promise possession in 2–3 years but take 4–6 years or longer. Your money stays locked, and you may continue paying rent and EMIs.

 

2. Builder runs out of money

Construction could stop because of financial problems, poor sales, disputes, or unpaid contractors. In extreme cases, the project may become stalled or abandoned.

 

3. Quality may be compromised

The completed property might have seepage, cracks, poor fittings, inadequate ventilation, plumbing issues, or differences from the advertised specifications.

 

4. Layout or specifications change

The builder might change the floor plan, amenities, parking arrangements, open spaces, or other features, subject to applicable approvals and legal restrictions.

 

5. Legal or land-title disputes

The land could have ownership disputes, mortgages, litigation, missing approvals, or restrictions that affect construction and possession.

 

6. Amenities and infrastructure never arrive

Promised roads, lifts, parking, gardens, water supply, drainage, electricity, or community facilities may be delayed or delivered differently than advertised.

2. Financial risks that people often overlook

Price escalation: Additional charges for parking, maintenance deposits, electricity connections, club membership, GST where applicable, and other items.

Loan complications: Your bank may approve a loan initially, but construction delays can create repayment pressure.

Resale difficulties: Selling an under-construction property can be harder than selling a completed, ready-to-move-in flat.

Opportunity cost: Your money remains invested in an asset that may not generate rental income for years.

Refund problems: If you cancel, recovering your booking amount may be difficult depending on the agreement and applicable law.

13.q: The builder says possession in 12 months. How do I check if that is believable?
13.text:
If a builder promises possession within 12 months, don't rely on the sales team's verbal assurance. You need to establish whether the project is actually at a stage where handing over a legally occupiable property within a year is realistic.

The best approach is to check three things:

Legal readiness: Are all approvals and permissions in place?

Construction progress: Has enough work already been completed to make the deadline realistic?

Builder's track record: Has this builder delivered previous projects on time?

Here's how I'd investigate before paying a booking amount or signing an agreement.

1. Check the project's legal status

Ask the builder for copies of:

RERA registration certificate and project registration number, if applicable.

Approved building plan.

Land title documents and ownership records.

Building permission and commencement permission.

Environmental and other statutory clearances, where applicable.

The sanctioned completion and possession schedule.

Important: Check the possession date registered with RERA, not just the date in the builder's brochure.

2. Check actual construction progress

Visit the site yourself. Ideally, take an independent civil engineer or architect with you.

 

Foundation stage

If excavation or foundation work is still underway, a 12-month possession promise is generally aggressive.

 

Structural stage

Check whether the building's full structural framework is complete.

 

Finishing stage

Plastering, wiring, plumbing, flooring, lifts, windows and internal finishing should be progressing.

 

Handover stage

Check utilities, fire safety requirements, access roads, common areas and occupancy/completion approvals.

A building looking nearly complete doesn't necessarily mean it is legally ready for possession.

3. Check the builder's previous delivery record

Ask these questions:

Which three projects has the builder completed in the last five years?

What were their original promised possession dates?

When were keys actually handed over?

Did buyers receive occupancy/completion certificates?

Are there unresolved complaints or litigation involving delayed possession?

Speak to at least three existing buyers, preferably people who purchased directly from the builder.

4. Check the RERA progress reports

If the project is RERA-registered, compare the quarterly progress reports with the actual site condition.

Look for:

Percentage of construction completed.

Work completed versus work scheduled.

Pending approvals.

Revised completion dates.

Any extensions or complaints.

Compensation or interest for delayed possession.

Refund and cancellation conditions.

Have a property lawyer independently review it before signing.

14.q: If the builder gets delayed by 2 years, what do I lose and what are my rights?
14.text:
If your builder delays handing over your property by 2 years beyond the promised possession date, you may have significant financial and legal rights. You do not necessarily have to accept the delay or simply wait.

Assuming your property is in Jammu & Kashmir, India, the key issue is whether the project is covered by RERA and what your Builder-Buyer Agreement says.

1. What do you lose if possession is delayed by 2 years?

There are several possible losses:

Rent: You may have to continue paying rent for two additional years.

Loan interest: If you have a home loan, you may continue paying interest or EMIs without getting possession.

Opportunity cost: Your money remains tied up in a property you cannot use or rent out.

Property value: You lose the opportunity to use, sell or rent the property during the delay.

Financial uncertainty: Construction costs, maintenance charges and other expenses may change.

You may be entitled to compensation for certain losses, depending on the law, agreement and circumstances.

2. What are your rights under RERA?

Under India's Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, Section 18 is particularly important.

If the builder fails to complete the project or give possession by the agreed date:

Option A — Withdraw from the project

You can seek a refund of the amount paid.

You can claim prescribed interest.

You may also have grounds to claim compensation.

Option B — Continue with the project

You can remain in the project.

You are entitled to interest for every month of delay until possession is handed over, as prescribed under applicable RERA rules.

You do not automatically lose these rights just because the builder says construction is delayed.

3. Can the builder escape responsibility?

Not simply by announcing a delay.

The builder may rely on genuine force majeure circumstances or legally permitted extensions, depending on the facts. However:

Ordinary financial difficulties are not automatically a valid excuse.

Increased construction costs do not automatically cancel your rights.

Verbal promises of a new possession date do not necessarily amend your contractual rights.

The builder should be able to explain and substantiate the delay.

The original agreement and any valid extension of the project timeline are important.

+1

4. What should you do now?

I would recommend:

Keep your original Builder-Buyer Agreement and payment receipts.

Check the contractual possession date, including any grace period.

Check the project's RERA registration and revised completion date.

Send the builder a written notice asking for a firm possession date and an explanation.

Claim the applicable delay interest under Section 18.

If the builder refuses, consider filing a complaint before the relevant RERA authority.

You may also have consumer-law remedies, depending on the circumstances.

+1

I can help assess your actual financial loss and legal position, rather than just explain the law generally.

Where is the property? Srinagar, Jammu, or somewhere else?

What type of property? Apartment, independent house, villa, or plot?

What was the promised possession date? For example, December 2025.

How much have you paid to the builder? Approximate amount in ₹ is fine.

Also, is the builder now saying possession will be delayed by another two years, or has the original possession date already passed?

With these details, I can work out:

Whether you can demand a full refund with interest.

Whether you can claim compensation in addition to interest.

Whether you should continue paying instalments or challenge further demands.

One important point: A two-year delay does not mean you must simply absorb two years of financial loss. You have legal remedies, and you should understand their value before agreeing to any revised possession date.

H4.q: Under-construction flat abhi book karu to kya risk hai?
H4.text:
Under-construction flat अभी बुक करना फायदेमंद हो सकता है, क्योंकि ready-to-move flat के मुकाबले कीमत कम मिल सकती है और payment construction के हिसाब से होती है। लेकिन इसमें कुछ बड़े risks भी हैं।

मेरी सलाह: बिना कुछ चीजें verify किए booking amount मत देना।

Under-construction flat बुक करने के 8 बड़े जोखिम

1. Possession में देरी: बिल्डर 2028 में possession देने का वादा करे, लेकिन प्रोजेक्ट 2029–30 तक भी पूरा न हो।

2. Builder का दिवालिया होना: पैसे लेने के बाद बिल्डर आर्थिक परेशानी में आ जाए या काम बंद कर दे।

3. RERA की समस्या: प्रोजेक्ट RERA में registered न हो या approvals में कमी हो।

4. Construction quality: तैयार होने पर दीवारों में cracks, leakage, खराब plumbing या कमजोर finishing मिल सकती है।

5. कीमत बढ़ने का जोखिम: GST, maintenance, parking, club charges और अन्य hidden charges के कारण कुल कीमत बढ़ सकती है।

6. Bank loan का जोखिम: बैंक से loan approval मिलने का मतलब यह नहीं कि प्रोजेक्ट पूरी तरह सुरक्षित है।

7. Carpet area का अंतर: Brochure में बड़ा flat दिखाया जाता है, लेकिन actual usable area कम हो सकता है।

8. Resale में मुश्किल: Construction पूरा होने से पहले flat बेचना कभी-कभी मुश्किल होता है।

RERA registration certificate और उसकी validity।

Land title और ownership documents।

Approved building plan और building permission।

Bank का project approval और legal clearance।

Builder के पिछले projects और delivery record।

Written agreement में possession date और delay compensation।

Total cost sheet जिसमें सभी अतिरिक्त charges शामिल हों।
